subtitle: A limestone quarry road opened this cliff-sealed Bukit Peninsula cove to the public in 2012, and visits reached 1.36 million a year within five years.
spike_statement: A rock quarry became the only road into this cliff-sealed Bali cove in 2012; annual visits hit 1.36 million by 2017, then crashed 44% in 2020.

levers.photo_tone: Gold-white quarried limestone walls, six weathered Pandava figures carved into the cliff, jade-shallow water striped with seaweed-farming lines, midday tour-bus crowds on the sand
